ai.literal: Because of the existence of the exceedingly great beauty called graciousness, this world exists.
ai.translation: This world continues to exist only because of the presence of that exceedingly great beauty called graciousness.
ai.modern: கண்ணோட்டம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் மிகச் சிறந்த அழகு இருப்பதனால்தான் இந்த உலகம் நிலைபெற்றுள்ளது.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that graciousness or kindly consideration is the ultimate beauty of human nature. The author describes this quality as an 'exceedingly great beauty' (கழிபெருங் காரிகை). The existence of the world and human society depends entirely on the presence of this virtue. Without empathy and benignity among people, social life would disintegrate, meaning the world exists only because of this grace.

ai.literal: In benignity exists the way of the world; the existence of those who do not have that is a burden to the earth.
ai.translation: The smooth running of the world rests on the quality of benignity; the very existence of those who lack it is but a burden to the earth.
ai.modern: உலக நடைமுறை கண்ணோட்டம் என்னும் பண்பில் தான் நிலைபெற்றுள்ளது; அப்பண்பு இல்லாதவர்களுடைய பிறப்பு இப்பூமிக்கு ஒரு பாரமே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme importance of kaṇṇōṭṭam (benignity, or a kindly, considerate outlook) for the sustenance of human society. The poet states that the orderly functioning and harmony of the world (ulakiyal) exist only because of this quality of kindness. For those who lack this gentle, sympathetic disposition (aḥtilār), their very existence (uṇmai) on this planet serves no positive purpose. Instead, they are described as a mere physical burden (poṟai) to the earth (nilakku), contributing nothing of value to the social fabric.

ai.literal: Melody what is the use to the song harmony if there is not? Eye what is the use benignity lacking eye?
ai.translation: What is the use of a melody if it has no harmony with the song? Likewise, what is the use of eyes if they lack benignity?
ai.modern: பாடலோடு பொருத்தம் இல்லை என்றால் இசையினால் என்ன பயன்? அதுபோல, இரக்கக் குணம் இல்லாத கண்களால் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a beautiful analogy to explain the true purpose of sight. A musical melody is meaningless if it does not harmonize with the song being sung. Similarly, physical eyes are of no real use if they lack 'kaṇṇōṭṭam', which is the quality of benignity, compassion, and looking upon others with kindness. The author suggests that the physical organ of the eye only fulfills its true function when it is accompanied by a sympathetic heart.

ai.literal: Appearing as if they are present on the face, what use will they do merely by their physical measure, the eyes that are without benignity?
ai.translation: What is the use of eyes that merely appear to exist on the face, if they lack the essential quality of benignity and kind consideration?
ai.modern: முகத்தில் இருப்பது போலத் தோன்றினாலும், இரக்கமும் கண்ணோட்டமும் இல்லாத கண்கள் ஒருவருக்கு இருப்பதால் என்ன பயன் விளையும்?
ai.explanation: This couplet explores the true purpose of the eyes. The author argues that eyes are not defined merely by their physical presence on a person's face. If they lack 'kaṇṇōṭṭam'—which refers to a benign, compassionate, and kindly outlook towards others—they are completely useless. They exist only in appearance and fail to perform their true human function.

ai.literal: To the eye, the ornament is benignity; if that is absent, it will be understood as a sore.
ai.translation: The true ornament of the eye is benignity; if that is lacking, those eyes will be regarded as mere sores.
ai.modern: கண்ணுக்கு உண்மையான அணிகலன் கண்ணோட்டம் (இரக்கம்) ஆகும்; அது இல்லை என்றால், அந்த கண்கள் வெறும் புண்கள் என்றே கருதப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true purpose and beauty of the eyes. The author states that the real ornament of an eye is 'kaṇṇōṭṭam', which means benignity, kind consideration, or a sympathetic outlook. If this quality of kindness is absent, the eyes lose their value and are to be regarded merely as sores or wounds on the face. Through this stark contrast, the couplet emphasizes that physical eyes without compassion are useless and unsightly.

ai.literal: With the earth connected, like trees they are, who, though connected with eyes, do not show kindliness.
ai.translation: Those who possess eyes but do not look upon others with kindliness are like trees that are merely fixed to the earth.
ai.modern: கண்களைப் பெற்றிருந்தும் பிறரிடம் இரக்கம் காட்டாதவர்கள், மண்ணோடு பொருந்தி நிற்கும் மரங்களைப் போன்றவர்கள் ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the importance of benignity or kindliness (kaṇṇōṭṭam). The author compares people who lack this quality to inanimate trees. Although they have eyes and are physically alive, their lack of empathy and kind looks makes them no better than wooden trees rooted in the soil. The word kaṇṇōṭṭam literally means the 'running of the eye' towards others in compassion; without this movement of grace, the eyes are mere physical organs, and the human is reduced to a stationary, unfeeling tree.

ai.literal: Those who lack kind consideration are without eyes; those who possess eyes, even the absence of kind consideration is not there for them.
ai.translation: Those who lack kind consideration have no eyes; for those who truly possess eyes, the absence of kind consideration is impossible.
ai.modern: கண்ணோட்டம் இல்லாதவர்கள் கண் இல்லாதவர்கள் ஆவர்; கண் உடையவர்கள் என்பவர்களிடம் கண்ணோட்டம் இல்லாமல் இருப்பது இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines what true eyes are by linking them to the quality of 'kaṇṇōṭṭam' (kind consideration or benignity). The author states that those who do not show kind consideration to others are effectively blind, lacking real eyes. Conversely, those who are said to possess eyes will never be without this quality of kind consideration. The play on the word 'kaṇ' (eye) and 'kaṇṇōṭṭam' (the flow of the eye, i.e., kindness) emphasizes that the physical organ is useless without its corresponding moral virtue.

ai.literal: To those who are capable of showing kindness without ruining their duty, this world possesses ownership.
ai.translation: This world belongs as a rightful possession to those who are capable of showing gracious kindness without letting their duties fall apart.
ai.modern: தங்கள் கடமை கெடாமல் பிறரிடம் இரக்கம் காட்ட வல்லவர்களுக்கு, இந்த உலகம் சொந்தமாகும் உரிமை உடையது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the delicate balance between duty (karumam) and kindness (kannottam). While showing gracious compassion to others is a great virtue, it must not be done at the cost of ruining one's essential duties. Those rare individuals who can successfully balance both—remaining kind and compassionate without compromising their responsibilities—earn the respect of everyone. To such balanced people, this entire world rightfully belongs.

ai.literal: Even towards those of the character of doing harm, showing consideration and practicing endurance is the supreme quality.
ai.translation: Even towards those whose nature is to cause harm, showing consideration and practicing forgiveness is the supreme virtue.
ai.modern: துன்பம் செய்யும் குணம் உடையவர்களிடத்தும் இரக்கம் காட்டி, அத்துன்பத்தைப் பொறுத்துக் கொள்ளும் பண்பே மிகச் சிறந்ததாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the ultimate expression of 'kaṇṇōṭṭam' (benignity or consideration). The poet states that it is easy to be kind to those who are good, but the supreme virtue lies in showing consideration even to those whose very nature is to cause harm. Instead of retaliating, one must look upon them with a kindly eye and endure their actions with patience. This noble quality of combining consideration with forgiveness is hailed as the highest of all virtues.

ai.literal: Even when poured and seeing it, poison having consumed they will remain composed, those who desire desirable benignity.
ai.translation: Those who desire the highly esteemed virtue of benignity will calmly drink even poison, even when they see it being poured out for them.
ai.modern: விரும்பத்தக்க கண்ணோட்டத்தை (நாகரிகத்தை) விரும்புகின்றவர்கள், தமக்கு நஞ்சை ஊற்றுவதைக் கண்ணால் கண்டபோதும் அதை உண்டு அமைதியாக இருப்பார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the ultimate limit of 'kaṇṇōṭtam' (benignity or consideration for others), which is here referred to as 'nākarikam' (civility or social refinement). Those who cherish this noble quality ('nākarikam vēṇṭupavar') value their relationships so highly that they would rather suffer than cause distress to others. Even if they openly see poison being served to them by someone, they will calmly drink it to avoid embarrassing or offending the host. The word 'nayattakka' emphasizes that this level of courtesy is highly desirable and worthy of praise.
